estimate.damage_summary: A nearby thunderstorm caused an overvoltage event that physically damaged a speaker system and a TV connected to the building’s electrical installation. A technician later confirmed the surge failure and checked wiring safety; the description says the equipment was not connected through surge protection.
estimate.policy_notes: The appliance class is covered for lightning-related overvoltage, subject to a EUR 5,000 VAT-inclusive event sub-limit and the pre-loss standard. Because the appliances were not connected through surge-protection devices, the policy reduces otherwise payable indemnity for them by half; this is a reduction, not an exclusion. Replacement-equipment delivery and installation are excluded, as are diagnostic and administrative outlays that are not repair costs. Attendance charges are excluded where the invoice does not also bill indemnifiable work.

lines.rationale: The description establishes physical surge damage to both appliances, making them plausibly covered and related, subject to the appliance sub-limit and 50% reduction for missing surge protection. The quantity of two matches the TV and speaker system; the estimate assumes equivalent standard-grade replacements rather than upgrades.

lines.invoice_text: Diagnostic surge-failure report and technician call-out
lines.rationale: The attendance and diagnostic visit relate to the reported event, but the described purpose was to confirm failure and check wiring safety, not to carry out a repair. Under the policy, diagnostic outlay is not a repair cost and the attendance charge is not payable on an invoice without indemnifiable work; the three-unit quantity is also not substantiated as three separate visits or services.

estimate.damage_summary: A nearby atmospheric discharge caused an overvoltage surge through the building mains, physically damaging a speaker system and TV in the dwelling. The technician later documented the surge failure and checked the wiring.
estimate.policy_notes: The appliances are eligible for overvoltage cover, subject to the EUR 5,000 VAT-inclusive aggregate appliance sub-limit and the no-improvement rule. Because the description establishes that the equipment was not connected through a surge-protective device, the policy halves the otherwise payable indemnity for the affected appliances; this is a reduction, not a complete exclusion. Diagnostic/reporting and attendance costs are not repair costs unless the attendance-charge exception applies to indemnifiable work on the same invoice.

lines.invoice_text: Surge-damaged home electronics (speaker system and TV set)
lines.rationale: Both appliances are identified as physically damaged by the insured overvoltage event, so replacement in equivalent pre-loss standard is related and covered, subject to the appliance sub-limit. No surge-protective device is established, so the otherwise payable amount is halved; the estimate allows for uncertainty about the appliances' original specification and the appropriate equivalent replacements.

lines.invoice_text: Diagnostic surge-failure report and technician call-out
lines.rationale: The report and wiring-safety check relate to the surge event, but diagnosis and confirmation alone do not make good physical damage and are not separately listed as insured costs. A call-out could qualify only if incurred on the occasion of indemnifiable work on the same invoice; this line describes a diagnostic attendance, not repair work, and the singular attendance described supports at most one unit if valid.

estimate.damage_summary: During a swerve on the Berlin–Munich drive, the laptop was thrown against the car door, cracking its screen and damaging its lower-right corner. The described sudden external impact and damage pattern are consistent with the portable-equipment cover; the pre-existing lid scuff is unrelated to the event.
estimate.policy_notes: The portable-equipment peril covers sudden external impact, including equipment displaced inside a vehicle, provided the peril and household contents are agreed in the schedule. Necessary repair costs are covered without an age deduction, subject to the sum insured and any sub-limit. The pre-existing scuff polish is excluded as unrelated cosmetic work. Necessary diagnostic examination is a covered cost, capped at EUR 250 including VAT per event; VAT is reimbursed only if actually incurred and not recoverable.

lines.rationale: The cracked screen is expressly reported as impact damage from the insured event, and replacing the complete display assembly is a plausible necessary repair where the glass is not separately serviceable.
